description: Human-reviewed exceptions for the Yellow dialogue coverage metric: a label whose own Yellow ROM extraction has no independent corpus match but that is proven harmless to leave untranslated, with a verified reason recorded per entry. Entries only credit the Yellow coverage *metric* for a label the dialogue layer itself intentionally leaves untranslated (see pipeline/builder.py's effective_dialogue_translated); they never derive or inject a translated *value* — that is config/rby/semantic_anchor_decisions.json's job, via the anchor extraction DSL.

_RoseText.rationale:
_RoseText, and its sibling ROM dialogue-catalog fragments _MonsStatsRoseText/_GreatlyRoseText/_GreatlyFellText, are leftover text-bank entries from the original cartridge (where the stock game engine printed several short text IDs back to back to build one line). Verified by reading src/battle/MoveEffects.lua (changeStage, the sole code path for every battle stat-stage message, moves and items alike): the recompiled engine does not read any of these four dialogue labels at runtime. It instead renders the message through four fixed Strings() engine-literal calls ("%s's
%s rose!", "%s's
%s
greatly rose!", "%s's
%s fell!", "%s's
%s
greatly fell!"), which are translated independently in overrides/it/rby/engine.json (reason: editorial-correction) and were confirmed present there. So _RoseText's own translation status has no effect on what the player sees; it is credited here as a known, harmless gap rather than a real missing translation to chase.
_RoseText.actual_render_mechanism:
overrides/it/rby/engine.json entries for "%s's
%s rose!", "%s's
%s
greatly rose!", "%s's
